title: A Crash Course on Boundaries
coreMove: A boundary is not a remote control for another person; it names the access you can allow, the action you will take, and the resentment you refuse to let build.

exampleSpecs.domain: public comment about a neighbor joining a private morning routine
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who wants to protect a personal ritual without shaming someone lonely
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether care for an elderly neighbor costs the quiet weekday walk that steadies the day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hyun uses Nancy's weekday morning walk and Saturday walk pattern while speaking at the town hall microphone stand

exampleSpecs.domain: physical therapy patient asking for a pressure limit during a stretch
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who apologizes before naming a body limit
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether pain becomes information or the patient performs toughness for approval
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Severin and Lana use the medium-well burger comparison to make a body limit sound as plain as a clear order

exampleSpecs.domain: teacher setting terms for grade-update calls and emails
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who thinks more explanation will prevent pushback
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether dread before a phone call becomes a clear access rule or another week of avoidance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Peyton expects a long explanation to reduce resentment, then sees the parent debate the reasons instead of hearing the limit

exampleSpecs.domain: food truck owner handling a friend's texts during lunch rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader whose attention gets treated as always available
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a friendship gets special access while customers wait at the window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Milo protects time and attention by texting what access is available at the food truck service window

exampleSpecs.domain: community garden volunteer ending repeated last-minute tool requests
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who piles on reasons until the limit disappears
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one clear sentence protects the plot or resentment keeps growing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hugo interrupts his routine at the community garden plot, stops overexplaining, and restarts with a direct limit

exampleSpecs.domain: apartment laundry room moment after an avoided family call
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who treats irritation as a personality flaw instead of information
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next call gets avoided again or becomes a clearer access conversation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lana notices dread, avoidance, resentment, and the phone call while cleaning the laundry room lint screen
